description:
Kernel.send is specced (pid | integer, t) but the extern it forwards to, fz_send, is (pid, t). The extern is right: a pid is an opaque value from self() or spawn; the integer in send's spec lets programs address a process by its runtime index (send(1, ...)), which is not part of the language (Elixir's send never takes an integer).

Change: @spec send(pid, t) :: t when t: any. User send(1, 42) becomes a compile-time spec/violation. Rewrite the 23 integer sends across 17 fixtures to thread real pids (parent = self() passed or captured; child = spawn(...) then send(child, x)); Kernel's @doc example becomes Kernel.send(self(), 42); specs.md's 'integer addressing is part of the callee's real domain' paragraph and the @doc raw-index sentence go. send_dead_unknown_pid's never-issued-pid assertion cannot be written with unforgeable pids (owner decision).

Tests that assert on these fixtures' compiled structure (transport_contract_test multi_relay, drive_test:5442, port_* tests) are checked against their intent; a rewrite that loses the shape a test covers is reported, not loosened.

Acceptance: failing-first numbered error fixture for send(1, 42) on all three doors; every rewritten fixture keeps its expected output on interp/JIT/AOT; moved pins listed with cause, rises reported; gate at baseline. Proposal: ../fz-xxd.2.html
title: send's receiver is a pid
